text.name: TextDesc2
text.text: The NEC PC-FX was released in 1994 as the successor to the PC Engine and SuperGrafx platforms. It used a CD-ROM format and focused heavily on animated graphics, video playback, and visual novel-style games. Unlike many competing fifth-generation consoles, it did not use polygon-based 3D hardware. Its library included titles such as Battle Heat, Zenki, and Farland Story FX. The PC-FX was released only in Japan and had a short commercial lifespan.
